Introduced by Google in May 2017 with Android 8.0, Project Treble is a major re-architecture of the Android OS framework designed to make updating devices to newer Android versions easier, faster, and less costly [1]. It aims to streamline the development and deployment of updates and address criticisms regarding short software support lifespans [2].

Project Treble achieves this by separating the vendor implementation from the Android OS framework using a new vendor interface [1]. This stable interface provides access to the hardware-specific parts of Android, allowing device makers to deliver new Android releases simply by updating the OS framework without needing additional work from silicon manufacturers [1].

Semantic search denotes search with meaning, whereas lexical search involves the search engine looking for literal matches of the query words or variants of them without understanding the overall query's meaning [1]. 

Semantic search improves search accuracy by understanding the searcher's intent and contextual term meaning using vector embeddings [1]. In contrast, lexical search relies on exact keyword or close textual matches [1][5].

Deepfakes are images, videos, or audio edited or generated using AI-based tools, artificial intelligence, or audio-video editing software [1]. The term itself is a portmanteau of "deep learning" and "fake" [1].

They can depict either real or fictional individuals and are categorized as synthetic media, which is typically created by combining various media elements into a new artifact using artificial intelligence systems [1].

Algorithmic bias describes a systematic and repeatable harmful tendency in computerized sociotechnical systems to create unfair outcomes, such as privileging one category or arbitrary group over another [1][2]. This bias can result in errors and unfair treatment, and it may be either intentional or unintentional [1][2].

The phenomenon can emerge from various factors, including deliberate design decisions or unanticipated uses and choices regarding how data is collected, coded, selected, or trained [1]. It can also occur when an AI has a predisposition toward certain answers based on the data it was trained on, resulting in skewed or non-objective responses [4].

Prompt engineering is the process of structuring natural language inputs, known as prompts, to produce specified outputs from a generative AI model [1]. It can also be defined as designing and refining input instructions given to a generative AI model to achieve more accurate, relevant, or useful outputs [1]. 

The Oxford English Dictionary defines it as the action or process of formulating and refining prompts for an artificial intelligence program or algorithm to optimize its output or achieve a desired outcome, as well as the profession or discipline concerned with this [2].

An AI hallucination is a response generated by an artificial intelligence that contains false or misleading information presented as fact [1]. These responses can include plausible-sounding random falsehoods, such as fabricated citations [1]. 

The term is also used to describe nonsense and misinformation presented as fact by large language models and chatbots [3]. In computer vision, it can refer to adding detail to an image to improve it or the erroneous detection of non-existent objects [2].

The offices were originally planned as Rive files, but two problems caused the project to switch to GSAP [1][2]. First, Claude, the coding assistant that helped build the project, cannot edit Rive files, meaning every single change had to go through Kenneth [1][2]. Second, Rive files can only switch between scenes drawn in advance, whereas the project needed to draw real data, such as one card per real chunk [1][2]. 

Instead, the project used flat SVG files animated in code with the GSAP library [1]. Kenneth tested this approach with a spike, building the Upload and Ask cycles in GSAP on a flat SVG, which proved that the method worked [2].
